## A matrix unit against the arithmetic pipe

16x16x16 a tile, which is 4096 multiply-adds — 128 for each of the warp's 32 lanes.

| Tiles | Route | Instructions | Warp steps | Lane ops | Cycles |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | fma | 129 | 129 | 4,128 | 513 |
| 1 | mma | 2 | 2 | 544 | 33 |
| 4 | fma | 513 | 513 | 16,416 | 2049 |
| 4 | mma | 5 | 5 | 2,080 | 129 |
| 16 | fma | 2049 | 2049 | 65,568 | 8193 |
| 16 | mma | 17 | 17 | 8,224 | 513 |

Priced at 16, the matrix instruction would have to cost 128 a lane before the
two routes came level — which is exactly the multiply-adds it performs. The
ratio between those two numbers is the claim being made about the unit, and
it is the only number here that is not counted.
